description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics — Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy — for a large language model’s performance after incorporating external feedback. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.86 to 1.00 in linear increments of 0.01, representing the model’s self-assessed confidence in its initial response. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear steps of 0.2, indicating the proportion of correct responses. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which remains consistently high across all confidence levels, hovering just below 1.0 (e.g., ~0.93 at 0.86, ~0.99 at 0.97, ~0.98 at 1.00), showing minimal variation. The green dashed line with square markers, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” starts at approximately 0.65 at 0.86, rises steadily to a peak of ~0.92 around 0.95–0.97, then declines to ~0.77 at 1.00, indicating that higher initial confidence does not always correlate with higher initial correctness. The orange dashed line with diamond markers, “Δ Accuracy” (change in accuracy), begins at ~0.29 at 0.86, decreases to a minimum of ~0.05 near 0.95, then rises again to ~0.22 at 1.00, suggesting that the model’s ability to improve via feedback is greatest at low and high confidence extremes and weakest in the mid-range. Error bars are present for all data points, indicating variability in measurements.
